# Taskbar Audio Spectrum 1.0.0

This first release turns the native Windows 10 or Windows 11 taskbar search box
into a real-time system-playback spectrum.

## Highlights

- Portable x64 standalone application and CMake-generated Windhawk mod source
- WASAPI loopback capture with automatic default-device reconnection
- Third-octave, Bark, logarithmic, Mel, and linear frequency layouts
- Configurable FFT size, windows, aggregation, frequency weighting, smoothing,
  colors, peak markers, silence hiding, DPI-aware offsets, and Windows startup
- Per-monitor DPI handling and recovery after Explorer or Search restarts
- Event-driven registry, foreground-window, and UI Automation tracking with
  cached geometry and low-frequency safety refreshes
- Recoverable settings reloads even when a stale shell call exceeds the
  bounded shutdown period
- Strict JSON validation, detailed logging, automated tests, and diagnostics

## Downloads

- `TaskbarAudioSpectrum-v1.0.0-win64.zip` — portable standalone package
- `TaskbarAudioSpectrum.exe` — standalone executable
- `taskbar-audio-spectrum.wh.cpp` — generated source for Windhawk
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — SHA-256 checksums for every release artifact

Windhawk users should compile the generated `.wh.cpp` source through Windhawk;
the release intentionally contains no prebuilt Windhawk DLLs.

The taskbar Search setting must be the full **Search box**. This visualizer
reports relative digital playback power and is not a calibrated sound-level
meter.

See the [README](https://github.com/ShangHTao/TaskbarAudioSpectrum#readme),
[configuration reference](https://github.com/ShangHTao/TaskbarAudioSpectrum/blob/main/docs/Configuration.md),
and [troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/ShangHTao/TaskbarAudioSpectrum/blob/main/docs/Troubleshooting.md).
